Cross-Validate Bayesian Scale Models

Source: R/cross_validate_bayes.R
cross_validate_bayes.Rd

Refit a multiScale_bayes() model in each analysis split, then score the held-out observations with the posterior predictive density. Observations that share a predicted group, such as a held-out site or year, also share its random effect when they are scored.

Usage

cross_validate_bayes(
  formula,
  data,
  kernel_inputs,
  folds,
  scales = NULL,
  family = c("nbinom2", "poisson", "binomial", "gaussian"),
  row_id = NULL,
  priors = list(),
  method = c("slice", "sample", "laplace", "marginal"),
  fit_args = list(),
  assessment_group = NULL,
  new_scale_levels = c("sample", "error", "zero"),
  new_response_levels = c("sample", "error", "zero"),
  new_group_draws = 1L,
  bin_reference = c("training", "fixed"),
  seed = NULL,
  keep_fits = FALSE
)

Arguments

formula

Two-sided response formula in multiScale_bayes() syntax. Use a data column as the response, or cbind(successes, failures) for grouped binomial data. An I() wrapper is also accepted.

data

Data frame of raw observations and formula variables. Its unique row names identify observations in folds, even when several observations share one prepared point.

kernel_inputs

Prepared landscape inputs from kernel_prep() or kernel_prep_by_group(). For the default training-only rebinning, prepare kernel means with bin = TRUE and store_cell_data = TRUE (both defaults of kernel_prep()). Weighted SQ and fixed-radius metrics also use the raw cells.

folds

Uniquely named list of splits. Each split holds nonempty, disjoint character vectors analysis and assessment of row names of data, as returned by grouped_cv_folds() or spatial_cv_folds(). Every analysis set needs at least two observations.

scales

Named list of scale formulas, as in multiScale_bayes(). The default NULL estimates one shared scale per landscape predictor.

family

Response family, one of "nbinom2" (default) or "poisson" for counts, "binomial" for successes and trials, or "gaussian" for continuous outcomes.

row_id

Optional name of the column of data that holds prepared point IDs. The default NULL uses the row names of data as point IDs. Point IDs may repeat. They do not replace the unique row names that identify observations.

priors

Named list of prior settings passed to multiScale_bayes(). Set them before you look at any assessment outcome. The default list() uses the documented defaults.

method

Computation for every fold. The default "slice" needs no optional sampling packages. "sample" runs NUTS. "laplace" and "marginal" use the approximations, and an importance-corrected marginal fit is scored directly with its candidate weights.

fit_args

Named list of further fitting arguments for multiScale_bayes(), chosen from chains, iter, warmup, control, laplace_draws, and cores. Settings you leave out take the defaults of multiScale_bayes(). Folds always run one after another.

assessment_group

Optional name of a column of data that defines joint scoring blocks within each assessment split. The default NULL scores each whole assessment split as one block. Choose the blocks to match your prediction question before you see any assessment outcome.

new_scale_levels, new_response_levels

What to do with a group level that is absent from an analysis split, set separately for scale and response random effects. The default "sample" averages over new-group variation by simulation. "error" refuses an unseen level, and "zero" predicts at a zero deviation. Groups present in the analysis split keep their fitted effects.

new_group_draws

Positive integer number of new-effect simulations per posterior vector when unseen levels are sampled; default 1. Raise it to reduce the simulation error of the average over new groups. See "Compare models".

bin_reference

"training" (default) computes the representative bin distances from the unique analysis points of each fold and freezes them for its assessment points. It needs the raw cells, so it refuses inputs prepared with store_cell_data = FALSE, such as lean inputs from kernel_prep_by_group(). "fixed" uses the prepared bin distances as given, so lean inputs of kernel means work with it. Use "fixed" only when the supplied bins were fixed independently of all analysis and assessment data.

seed

Optional positive integer seed. It generates distinct fitting and scoring seeds for every fold, and your own random-number state is restored afterward.

keep_fits

Logical. The default FALSE stores compact fold records only. TRUE also keeps every fold's complete fit in fits, for investigation, at a cost in memory.

Value

An object of class multiScaleR_bayes_cv, which inherits from multiScaleR_cv (see multiScaleR_cv). It is a list with these elements.

  • summary: a one-row data frame with the pooled score. estimate is the sum of joint negative log scores divided by the number of assessment observations (unit is "joint_block_density_per_observation"), so lower is better. n_assessment, n_scored, weight_sum, and complete describe its basis. estimate is NA unless every fold scored.

  • metrics: the same score for each fold.

  • predictions: one row per assessed observation, with fold, row_id, point_id, observed, trials, assessment_group, the posterior mean response prediction (a per-trial probability for binomial models), marginal_neg_log_score for that observation alone, new_scale_level and new_response_level flags, and eligible, which is TRUE only in a scored fold.

  • joint_scores: one row per fold and assessment block, with its size n and joint neg_log_score.

  • fold_results: one row per fold, with n_analysis, n_assessment, and status, which is "scored", "diagnostic_failed", or "failed" (an error at any stage, recorded in errors).

  • diagnostics: for each fold, the fit's stored checks (raw), the diagnose_bayes_scales() report for sampled fits (derived), the overall passed flag, and the importance records of corrected fits.

  • errors, warnings: for each fold, the failing stage and message (or NULL), and the warnings captured during the fold.

  • training: for each fold, the analysis rows and point IDs, the fit and score seeds, the frozen normalization (center, spread, and those of fixed-radius metrics), the bin distances and their reference, and the priors.

  • prediction_contracts: for each fold, the unseen groups, the number of posterior vectors, new_group_draws, and whether importance weights were used.

  • targets, folds, settings, assessment_counts, complete, call, integrity_sha256: the scored observations, the validated splits, the settings, how often each row was assessed, whether every fold scored, the call, and a checksum that cv_tab() uses to detect altered records.

  • fits: the complete fold fits when keep_fits = TRUE, and NULL otherwise.

Details

This function is experimental. Its arguments and results may change in a later release without a deprecation period.

What the score measures

The joint score of a block is the negative log of the posterior average of the product of the observation densities in that block. Lower is better. New effects are drawn once per group in each joint parameter vector and shared by every assessment observation in that group. For grouped binomial data, each observation contributes one normalized probability of its count of successes. The sum of the marginal row scores is a different target. The pooled score weights each block by its number of observations. It is the only cross-validation score in the package that averages over uncertainty in the coefficients, the scales, and the group effects.

Choose folds for your prediction question

Each fit learns the normalization, formula bases, coefficients, and scales from its analysis rows only. Repeated visits can share one point buffer. To predict new sites or years, hold out whole sites or years, for example with grouped_cv_folds() on the site labels. Where groups cross, make each assessment block cover the observations whose joint response you want to predict. vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR") discusses fold design.

Handle failed folds

A fold that fails its native or derived diagnostics is marked "diagnostic_failed" and leaves the result incomplete, though its computed scores stay available for investigation. Slice sampling without the posterior package can score folds with diagnostics recorded as unavailable, so install posterior to check mixing and simulation precision. Laplace and marginal scores inherit the limits of their approximation and its checks. Importance-corrected fits are scored with their normalized candidate weights. Passing numerical checks does not establish predictive calibration. Every fold runs the full fitting method, so a run takes about as long as one fit per fold. When any fold is not scored, the function returns the result and gives one warning that counts the failed folds and quotes their first distinct reasons. Read errors for the stage and message of every failed fold.

Compare models

Use cv_tab() with metric = "neg_log_score" to rank complete Bayesian results computed on the same targets, folds, blocks, and new-level policies. Poisson and NB2 results can be compared, because both score probability mass on the same counts. Training AIC, AICc, and BIC selection does not apply to posterior fits, so use an outer split to evaluate a model-selection rule. The average over unseen group effects uses a finite number of simulated effects. When two candidates score very closely, rerun both with a larger new_group_draws and the same seed and fitting settings, and treat the comparison as unresolved if the ranking changes.

See also

multiScale_bayes(), grouped_cv_folds(), spatial_cv_folds(), diagnose_bayes_scales(), cv_tab(), multiScaleR_cv; vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR").

Examples

# \donttest{
data("landscape_counts")
data("surv_pts")
land <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",
                                package = "multiScaleR"))
# Keep the raw cells (the default) so each fold rebins from its own
# analysis points
inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = terra::vect(surv_pts), raster_stack = land[["land1"]],
                      max_D = 1700, kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE)

# Two folds of alternating rows
folds <- grouped_cv_folds(rep(1:2, length.out = nrow(landscape_counts)),
                          k = 2, ids = rownames(landscape_counts))

# Very short slice chains keep this example quick. With the posterior
# package installed, they usually fail the diagnostics, so the folds are
# marked "diagnostic_failed", the pooled score is NA, and a warning says
# so. Use the default chains and iter in an analysis.
cv <- cross_validate_bayes(counts ~ land1, landscape_counts, inputs, folds,
                           family = "poisson",
                           priors = list(scale_median = 300),
                           method = "slice",
                           fit_args = list(chains = 2, iter = 200), seed = 1)
#> Warning: cross_validate_bayes() returned an incomplete result: 2 of 2 folds failed, so the pooled scores are NA. Reason: "The fold did not pass its posterior diagnostics." (fold1, fold2). Inspect `$errors` of the result for the stage and message of every failed fold.
cv$fold_results    # status of each fold
#>    fold n_analysis n_assessment            status
#> 1 fold1         50           50 diagnostic_failed
#> 2 fold2         50           50 diagnostic_failed
cv$joint_scores    # joint negative log score of each assessment block
#>    fold assessment_group  n neg_log_score
#> 1 fold1       whole_fold 50      105.5412
#> 2 fold2       whole_fold 50       90.7778
cv$summary         # pooled score per observation, lower is better
#>          metric estimate                                unit n_assessment
#> 1 neg_log_score       NA joint_block_density_per_observation          100
#>   n_scored weight_sum complete
#> 1        0          0    FALSE
# }
